open-question.question: The dispatched provide-alternatives-to-open-question agent calls the open-question tool twice per run (one locate, one list --with-question) and is not among the five multi-call sites the goal names. Should core/agents/provide-alternatives-to-open-question.md also state the full-command rule (write the full command on every call, never through a variable, alias, or function of the runner's own), or is it left unchanged?
open-question.alternative: `core/agents/provide-alternatives-to-open-question.md` is not edited. The full-command rule stays at the five multi-call sites the goal names. The new `CLAUDE.md` invariant bullet describes the rule as it applies to those sites and does not mention the alternatives agent either way. It keeps the milestone at exactly the scope the goal set. The agent makes only two tool calls per run. They use different subcommands (`locate`, `list --with-question`), and each is already written out in full in its own fenced block. That is the setting least likely to tempt a runner into defining a variable or function to save typing. A failure there also costs little: the orchestrator's existing one-repair-then-skip pipeline already handles a bad return. The agent is the one tool-calling runner left without the rule, even though it calls the tool more than once and the Claude render of its command already holds an unquoted host variable. A dispatched agent that builds a command-prefix variable on a shell that does not split words would fail its grounding. That burns the dispatch's single repair, or drops the question to a skip in parallel runs. A later editor could also read the omission as an oversight, because nothing records that it was deliberate.

The agent file is not edited. The new `CLAUDE.md` invariant bullet explicitly names the `provide-alternatives-to-open-question` agent as outside the full-command rule. The reason it gives is that the agent makes only two distinct, fully written-out calls per run, not a repeated series of calls. This is the same treatment the bullet already gives the capture skill's snapshot variable. Runtime prose stays inside the goal's five named sites, and the boundary is still recorded. A later editor sees the omission was chosen and does not "fix" it back. This follows the precedent set by the Snapshot variable decision, which names an out-of-rule site in the rationale instead of leaving it silent. It carries the same runtime exposure as leaving the agent silent: a dispatched agent that builds a variable still fails on a non-splitting shell. It also adds a second carve-out sentence to the rationale bullet to justify a gap that one clause in the agent file would close. That makes the invariant longer while protecting nothing more at runtime.

`core/agents/provide-alternatives-to-open-question.md` gets the same full-command clause the five sites get, in the matching wording already decided ("write the full command shown on every call; never define a variable, alias, or function of your own to stand for it or any part of it"). It is stated once in the file, attached to the step-1 tool-contract sentence ("You reach `open_questions.xml` through exactly two calls …"), which already spells out the full command. Neither fenced call gets anything beside it, and the commands are untouched. The new `CLAUDE.md` invariant bullet counts the agent among the sites the rule is stated at. Every runner that calls the open-question tool more than once now carries the rule, the dispatched agent included. This matches the milestone's own precedent: the Agent staging decision extended the literal-path rule to the `complete-task` agent's own text, because an agent reads no extra file and a failure inside a dispatched context is the hardest to see. The agent reads its own file whole before its first call, so the clause is in front of it exactly when it would set up a variable. It goes past the goal's explicit list of five sites, adding a sixth runtime file and one more copy of the clause to keep in matching wording. The case is weaker than at the true multi-call sites: with only two different calls, the variable-building failure the milestone targets is the least likely here, so the edit may guard against a failure that never happens.

open-question.question: The goal names the runtime files, the CLAUDE.md invariants, and the rebuilt hosts/ trees as this milestone's deliverables and says nothing about docs/. Should any page under docs/ (for example the "How skills commit" section of docs/workflow.md or the entries of docs/skill-reference.md) describe the literal-path rule and the full-command rule, or do the docs stay unchanged?
